title: Triage playbook for model-quality regressions and CSR templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document explains the operational process for detecting, triaging, and recovering from model-quality regressions (MQRs) that materially affect customer-facing outputs. It includes runbook steps, ownership, on-call rotation guidance, game day scenarios for MQRs, postmortem checklist, and customer/CSR notification templates.

Scope:
- Applies to any regression that changes generation quality: hallucinations, large accuracy drops, safety/TOX outputs, or systematic formatting errors for production models served by Redwood.
- Excludes infra-only outages where model execution returns but request routing/latency is the primary cause; see latency playbooks for those flows.

Objectives:
1. Rapidly detect and contain regressions to minimize customer impact.
2. Provide clear ownership and escalation rules between Serving, Applied ML, and SRE.
3. Maintain transparent customer communication and post-incident learning.

Key contacts and ownership:
- First responder (FR): oncall serving-runtime engineer (primary)
- Applied ML triage lead (AMLT): Applied ML team member (secondary)
- SRE escalation owner: SRE oncall (tertiary)
- Customer success liaison (CSL): assigned CSR for impacted accounts
- Pager rotation: eng-sre oncall schedule (see /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations)

SLO and thresholds for triggering this playbook:
- Quality SLOs: measured per-eval-suite or per-customer prompt set. Trigger if:
  - Absolute metric drop > 8% (e.g., exact match/ROUGE/F1 depending on suite) over 1 hour compared to baseline, OR
  - Burst of customer complaints (>=3 distinct customers complaining about similar failure mode within 30 minutes), OR
  - Safety threshold breach: >1% toxic responses in production sampling window.

Automatic detection signals (examples):
- Canary evaluation failure (continuous eval alerts)
- Regression alerts from Redwood Optimize monitors (quality drift detector)
- Unexpected prompt-set eval failures after a rollout
- Customer reports via support channels tagged as "model-quality"

Immediate runbook (first 30 minutes):
1) Acknowledge and declare incident
   - FR acknowledges pager within 5 minutes. Set bridge (Zoom/Jira/Slack huddle) and incident Slack channel #incident-mqr-<id>.
   - Use incident classification: MQR-1 (safety-critical), MQR-2 (major quality degradation), MQR-3 (minor / localized).
2) Quick scope and containment
   - Collect sample failing inputs/outputs and timestamps.
   - Check last deploys/rollouts: matching model version, quantization profile, kernel changes, or routing rules in the last 24 hours.
   - If issue maps to a specific rollout/config change, immediately enact rollback to previous pinned model variant (see rollback checklist below).
3) Notify Applied ML and Customer Success
   - Ping AMLT and CSL on-call. Provide sample artifacts and initial classification.
4) Apply short-term mitigations (if rollback not feasible)
   - Route affected traffic to a fallback model variant (lower-recall but safer/older model) via smart routing rules.
   - Increase sampling and enable verbose logging for the impacted routes.

Rollback checklist (if root cause is a recent model or config change):
- Confirm baseline model hash/version to roll back to.
- Validate rollback model passes smoke evals (canary prompts).
- Ensure KV cache or prefix cache is invalidated appropriately if required.
- Coordinate with infra/SRE for deployment window (aim for immediate out-of-band rollback).
- Communicate rollback start in incident channel and to CSL for customer notices.

Deep triage (30–180 minutes):
- AMLT performs targeted evals on prompt sets showing failure modes.
- FR gathers system telemetry: model version, GPU nodes, kernel versions, quantization flags, and request routing metadata.
- SRE checks runtime logs for memory corruption, OOM patterns, or precision-induced anomalies.
- If a data-related issue is suspected (label drift, tokenizer changes), involve Data Platform and Product for evaluation.

Decision ladder for broadened escalation:
1) If rollback/fallback eliminates customer impact -> transition to recovery & monitoring.
2) If rollback not possible and impact > MQR-2 -> open major incident and include CTO/Head of Applied ML in bridge.
3) If safety-critical outputs present -> notify Legal and Security immediately and follow restricted comms path.

Customer and CSR communication templates
- Use these templates as plain text in Support and Status updates. Customize per customer severity and SLA. Always include: what happened, who is affected, what we're doing, and expected next update time.

Template A: Initial short notice (within 30–60 minutes)
Subject: [Redwood] Investigation under way for model output quality affecting [service]
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},
We’re contacting you because we are investigating an issue that may affect the quality of outputs from {ModelName} for requests sent after {ISOtimestamp}. Our engineers are actively investigating and we may route traffic to a fallback model to reduce incorrect or unsafe outputs. We will send another update within 60 minutes.
If you notice any critical safety issues, please contact your CSR immediately (direct line: {CSRPhone}).
– Redwood Operations

Template B: Follow-up notification (after rollback/fallback)
Subject: [Redwood] Mitigation applied for model quality issue affecting {ModelName}
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},
We applied a mitigation at {ISOtimestamp} that routes traffic for {ModelName} to a safe fallback variant while we complete root-cause analysis. Impacted requests should resume normal quality within the next 5–15 minutes. We will share a detailed incident report after the investigation completes.
– Redwood Operations & Applied ML

Template C: Post-incident summary (to customers and CSRs)
Subject: [Redwood] Incident report: model-quality regression for {ModelName} (incident {IncidentID})
Body:
Summary:
- Incident window: {Start} – {End}
- Affected models/routes: {ModelName}/{Route}
- Root cause: {Short description}
- Remediation: {Rollback / Fix applied}
- Customer impact: {Description and metrics}
- Mitigations taken: {List}
Next steps:
- Permanent fix ETA: {Date}
- Monitoring improvements: {List}
We appreciate your patience and will reach out to impacted accounts directly with any follow-up.
– Redwood Operations

Postmortem and learning checklist (owner: incident owner, due within 7 days):
1) Evidence collected: logs, eval run outputs, model hashes, sampling artifacts.
2) Timeline constructed with decision points and communications.
3) Root cause hypothesis and validation steps documented.
4) Action items defined with owners and deadlines (e.g., revert rollback automation, improve canary suite).
5) Add regression tests to eval harness and link to CI (owner AMLT).
6) Publish postmortem to Confluence and tag related pages.
7) If customer-facing, coordinate customer call scheduling with CS.

On-call rotation guidance specific to MQRs:
- Serving oncall: primary pager for 0–60 minutes after detection. Must be able to perform rollbacks and routing changes.
- AMLT oncall: secondary pager, expected to be available within 30 minutes for evals.
- SRE: tertiary pager for infra-related escalations.
- Shift handoff: include open incident ID, current classification, mitigation state, and outstanding postmortem tasks.

Game day scenarios (recommended quarterly):
1) Canary-eval regression after staged rollout: practice identifying failing prompts, performing rollback, and updating routing rules.
2) Safety spike simulation: generate synthetic toxic outputs and exercise restricted comms and Legal/Security handoffs.
3) Silent-degradation: only 5% of requests fail quality checks — test detection sensitivity and sampling rules.

Metrics and dashboards to monitor (minimum):
- Quality SLO score (per-route and global) with 5/15/60-minute windows.
- Canary evaluation pass rate (per-deploy).
- Customer complaint rate for model-quality tag.
- Fraction of traffic on fallback variants.

Runbook snippets (CLI / API)
- Route traffic to fallback variant (example):
  curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/routing/override -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"model-v1.3-fallback","duration_minutes":60}'

- Trigger immediate canary eval (example):
  redwood-eval run --suite=canary-small --model=model-v1.4 --output=canary-output.json

Operational improvements (post-incident backlog suggestions):
- Harden rollback automation to validate canary smoke tests automatically.
- Expand canary prompt sets to include recent customer prompts and safety-focused cases.
- Improve sample retention for quick evidence collection (increase to 24h for quality incidents).
- Add routing telemetry tag for every request to trace policy decisions.

Appendix A: Incident severity examples
- MQR-1 (Safety-critical): Generation yields unsafe content (toxicity, privacy leak) for multiple customers or a high-severity single-customer incident. Immediate Legal and Security involvement.
- MQR-2 (Major quality drop): Systematic accuracy drop impacting many customers; performance still usable but degraded.
- MQR-3 (Localized): Single-customer or single-route degradation with limited blast radius.

Appendix B: Evidence collection checklist
- Sample inputs and outputs (CSV/JSON)
- Model version/hash and rollout ID
- Eval outputs for canary and baseline
- Routing configuration at the time of incident
- Host/runtime telemetry (GPU logs, kernel versions)
